ai.definition: Perovskite-silicon tandems are a type of photovoltaic technology that combines perovskite and silicon layers to create highly efficient solar cells by capturing more of the solar spectrum.
ai.howItWorks: The perovskite layer, with its wide bandgap, captures high-energy blue photons, while the underlying silicon layer handles lower-energy red photons. This stacking allows for a broader range of light absorption compared to single-layer silicon cells.
ai.problemSolved: Improving the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of solar panels by utilizing perovskite materials that can capture more of the solar spectrum than traditional silicon alone.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves depositing thin layers of perovskite on top of a silicon substrate, typically through solution-based methods like spin coating or inkjet printing. This allows for potentially lower-cost production compared to traditional crystalline silicon processes.
ai.buildProcess: First, the silicon wafer is prepared and cleaned. Perovskite precursor solutions are then applied using techniques such as spin coating or slot-die coating. The perovskite film is annealed to form the desired crystal structure before additional layers of perovskite can be deposited for tandem cells.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the stability and efficiency of perovskites, which are still improving, and the scalability of production methods such as solution processing versus vacuum deposition techniques used in silicon manufacturing.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to continue maturing with improvements in stability and efficiency, leading to broader adoption in high-efficiency solar panel markets.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks for perovskite-silicon tandems are still developing. Current regulations focus on the environmental impact of perovskites during manufacturing and disposal, as well as safety concerns related to lead content in some perovskite formulations.
ai.risks: Environmental risks include the potential toxicity of perovskites, particularly those containing lead. Technical risks involve achieving stable performance over long periods and integrating perovskites with silicon without degradation issues.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently limited by higher R&D costs and lower production volumes but is expected to improve as manufacturing processes become more established and efficiency gains are realized.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on enhancing the stability of perovskite materials, reducing cost through improved manufacturing techniques, and addressing environmental concerns related to lead content.

glossary.def: A class of materials with a specific crystal structure that can be used in solar cells due to their ability to absorb and convert light efficiently.

Photovoltaic cells composed of multiple layers, each optimized for different parts of the solar spectrum. In perovskite-silicon tandems, this means combining silicon with a perovskite layer to capture more light.
